_comment: Gameplay QA inventory. Every gameplay system must be listed here with at least one automated test or an explicit gap; Tools/check_qa_inventory.py scans the sources (UCLASS/UINTERFACE classes, Core headers, Spn.* console commands, Default*Key bindings) and fails when something is not listed. Add new features here when you add them (the QA script refuses to run otherwise). Regenerate Docs/Development/Gameplay-QA-Inventory.md with: check_qa_inventory.py --write
ignore_note: Variant_* are the Unreal template sample variants (Combat, Platforming, SideScrolling): not SPN gameplay, not part of the SPN game modes, neither used nor tested here.

entries.title: Gaits Walk/Jog/Run/Sprint, acceleration, braking, gait cycle and sprint keys
entries.gap: Gamepad sprint (DefaultSprintGamepadKey) and analog stick magnitudes through a real gamepad are not tested; speeds are the current placeholder values, not approved tuning.

entries.title: Direction changes, 90/180 degree turns, sprint left/right
entries.gap: The steering model of the Core (GroundSteering) is not wired into the Unreal movement yet; SprintTurn fails until that decision is made (see Docs/Development/M2A2-Windows-Integration-Report.md).

entries.title: Jump: standing, moving, sprint, ledges, collisions, landing
entries.gap: Jump key is bound by the template's IMC_Default asset (Space), exercised through SpnQA.Jump but not inventoried as a C++ binding; coyote time / jump buffering do not exist.

entries.title: Obstacles, steps, stairs and ramps
entries.gap: Obstacles and StairsAndRamps fail today (walking over 30 cm ledges, 30 cm stairs); a capsule/step decision by the developer is open.

entries.title: Ledge assist: step on, vault, mantle, climb up (explicit jump input, bands 40 / 120 / 180 cm)
entries.gap: No animation (the capsule follows the core path; the mesh plays the jump pose). Network prediction of a running move is not done (single player only). Tested on runtime boxes on the movement test map, not on the generated world's walls and fences.

entries.title: Sprint/gait prediction and replay for network play
entries.gap: No real multi-client session with latency is run; co-op networking is not designed yet.

entries.title: Opt-in movement frame recorder (spn.MoveDiag)
entries.gap: Developer tool; measured through the report tests, no pass/fail assertion on the recorder format itself.

entries.title: Play-area guard and reset points
Follow camera: collision, arm recovery, mesh hiding, tight spaces
entries.gap: Camera look input (mouse/stick sensitivity) and field-of-view behaviour are not tested; there is no automated visual comparison of what the camera shows.

entries.title: Interaction trace, reach and the E key
entries.gap: No on-screen prompt or highlight exists, so nothing visible to test; interaction through a gamepad button is not bound. InteractionSystem V2 (selection, statuses, cooldowns, links, events) is Core only and not yet used by USpnInteractionComponent; no Unreal test of it exists.

entries.title: Doors: open/close via E, swing, collision, persistence
entries.gap: Locked doors have no key model; door sound/animation are placeholders. Closing onto a player: the Core decides through a block rule, but the Unreal overlap query (ASpnTestDoor) is written without a build and NOT verified; doors vs NPCs: checked headless since NightBuild06 (an NPC standing in the swing); NPCs walking through doors are not tested. Step-aside (2026-11-13): the character that opened a door and stands in its swing takes one short walked step out of it if a capsule sweep finds room, else the door stays blocked; the step direction is the shortest of several candidates (radial, straight back, 15 degree steps; never towards the leaf) that passes the capsule sweep and ends on walkable floor. SpnGame.Doors.Walked* tick a headless world so the character really walks (open space, 140 cm corridor, dead end, pawn behind, ledge, capsule radius 25/35/50/60); StepAsideMargin 12 / MaxLength 90 are placeholders. Not covered: stairs at the door, moving obstacles appearing during the step (only the no-progress stop handles them). 2026-11-24 (NightBuild06): a real ASpnNpc in the swing stops the leaf, is never moved or asked to step, and blocks closing (SpnGame.Doors.NpcInTheSwingIsNeverPushed); the opener step clears the leaf with the default, test_160_fit and test_195_fit capsules.

entries.title: Pickups and inventories
entries.gap: The V2 level contains no pickups (they live in the M1 test maps); there is no inventory UI.

entries.title: World state (facts), save and load
entries.gap: Player position/character state, a save menu, quick-save and autosave do not exist (reported as NOT_IMPLEMENTED by SpnQA.SaveLoad). Object-state persistence (changed-state records, regions, atomic files) is Core only and not wired to USpnWorldStateSubsystem.

entries.title: Game mode, player controller, PlayerStart and single player pawn
entries.gap: The V2 level places no NPC pawn, so SpnQA.Spawn reports npc_vs_player as NOT_TESTED there; NPC pawns (ASpnNpc, NightBuild05) are spawned and checked in suite Npc (Lvl_SpnNpcTest) and SpnWorldQA.Route. Local split-screen/co-op spawning is not designed.

entries.title: Map V2 generator output, instancing and buildings
entries.gap: Window gaps, street crossings and lighting are only checked visually (screenshots/video); load time and editor viewport performance are not measured. The opt-in enriched level (Lvl_SpnMovementTestV2Env, spn_env_enrichment.py) exists only as generator data and Fedora-side geometry validation; nothing of it was generated or seen in Unreal (see Docs/Development/M2A3-Environment-Visual-Checklist.md).

entries.title: Frame time, draw calls, memory
entries.gap: No approved performance budget exists; SpnQA.Performance uses a placeholder (30 FPS average, worst frame below 100 ms).

entries.title: NPC, appearance, detail tiers and content ids (engine-independent Core only)
entries.gap: These Core modules are not integrated in the Unreal game, so there is no in-game test; the Core tests are CMake/CTest tests (Fedora) and are NOT run by the Windows QA script.

entries.title: Investigation: evidence, dialogue, investigation assists, case prototype (engine-independent Core only)
entries.gap: Core only (SPN-DEV-02/03, merged from main 2026-11-25): no Unreal witness actor, evidence object or journal UI yet (Docs/Planning/TASKS.md UNREAL-WITNESS-EVIDENCE), so nothing is checked in game. PROTOTYPE-CASE-01 is a placeholder closure rule (witness AND evidence), closure stays a manual player action (EVD-04/05). Planned use: the first case proposal Docs/Proposals/0019.

entries.title: First case 'Die Stille Mühle', night build A (NightBuild07): blind creature hunting by sound, the bell, throwables, player death / respawn with the difficulty's health, autosaves, save block during a pursuit, difficulty profiles, the greybox case level
entries.gap: PLACEHOLDER case (Docs/Proposals/0019, Docs/NightBuild07): engine shapes, no sound, no animation; the developer makes the assets later. Headless tests tick a small world without a navigation mesh (the creature steers straight); SpnCaseQA.Mill checks the generated level Lvl_SpnCaseMill (content, the navigation the creature needs, the player's ways) and takes 4 screenshots in a rendered -game run - not a playtest. SpnCaseQA.Flow (rendered -game run from the main menu) covers New game -> the arrival autosave -> death -> the death screen (Back does not close it) -> 'Load the last checkpoint' -> alive at the autosave with the difficulty's health, and the disabled Save entry of the pause menu while the creature hunts. NOT covered yet: the second autosave point (before_mill_night) in a walked run, a real catch in the level (the flow test kills by DamagePlayer), a picked bottle is not saved (it comes back after a load), health is not saved, no crouch key exists (Walk is the quiet gait). Values are placeholders (two TEST difficulty profiles only; DIF-01 count and names open). No manual playtest. The SpnCaseQA.* tests are deliberately not SpnQA.* (the QA runner would run them on its own maps; on 2026-11-26 that crashed a QA Full run before the rename) and are not part of run_gameplay_qa.ps1 yet.

entries.title: Switch, button, lever and links (Core foundation)
entries.gap: No Unreal actors or components exist for these devices; nothing is visible in a level. Only Core behavior is tested.

entries.title: World map domain: layers, regions, points of interest, markers, discovery, spatial queries (Core foundation, M2B1)
entries.gap: Not integrated in the Unreal game: no map data (the world geometry will come from SPN WorldForge), no UI and no save-game wiring. M2B3.3 added WorldMapState::Revision() (tested in Core, not saved, used by the snapshot guard) as preparation for the map save integration.

entries.title: Minimap calculations: world-to-screen transform, rotation modes, viewport clipping, off-screen indicators (Core foundation, M2B1)
entries.gap: Produces data only; no widget renders it and no Unreal coordinate adapter exists (axis mapping to Unreal is still to be defined). Only Core behavior is tested.

entries.title: Inventory domain: item definitions, stacks, containers, capacity, equipment slots, transactions (Core foundation, M2B1) and its Unreal integration USpnInventorySubsystem with a temporary data-driven test catalog and developer commands (M2B3.3)
entries.gap: M2B3.4: a UMG-ready view-model (USpnInventoryViewModel) and an optional presentation data asset class exist (the widget layer is the separate inventory.ui entry). M2B3.3: usable in a game session through developer commands only; no UI, no pickup/drop actors, no item content (the 6 test items and 3 container presets in Content/SpnTest/Inventory/TestItemCatalog.json are temporary test data), and the placeholder pickup counts in WorldFacts (Pickup.h) are still separate. The catalog is a JSON file, not yet a packaged data asset. Replication/host authority is not modelled. Saved through USpnSaveSubsystem as player.inventory.

entries.title: Graphical inventory screen (M2B3.5): UMG widgets over USpnInventoryViewModel with keyboard, mouse and gamepad input, DE/EN texts and a UI subsystem that opens/closes it and restores the input state
entries.gap: M2B3.5: the widget tests drive the screen through HandleKey() and read the real widget texts; the rendered session (open key, input-mode switch, mouse clicks, screenshots) is validated by the SpnQA.InventoryUi gameplay QA test. Not covered: a physical DualSense (gamepad input is simulated with gamepad key events), packaged builds, item icon textures (swatch fallback only).

entries.title: Navigation domain: destinations, route data model, route validation and measurement (Core foundation, M2B1)
entries.gap: Data model only: no pathfinding and no road graph (both come from WorldForge / Unreal navigation); nothing is shown in the game. Only Core behavior is tested.

entries.title: Canonical world coordinates and adapters: metres/east-north-up, Unreal centimetre axis presets, local frames, map and minimap (Core foundation, M2B2)
entries.gap: Axis preset is a PROPOSAL (master: open, WF-DC01 / CQ-101). M2B3.1 added a thin Unreal adapter (SpnWorldFrame) verified in the engine for yaw/axis directions and two test-map locations; no gameplay system uses it yet and it has not been checked against WorldForge output.

entries.title: Unified save slot: versioned sections, checksums, atomic publication with previous generation, game-state adapters (Core foundation, M2B2) and its Unreal integration USpnSaveSubsystem for WorldFacts (M2B3.2)
entries.gap: M2B3.2/3: WorldFacts and (while the inventory has a catalog) player.inventory are saved through the Unreal subsystem (Spn.SaveGame / Spn.LoadGame; the legacy Spn.SaveWorld / Spn.LoadWorld file is kept). Map and object sections have no Unreal owner: slots holding them are refused, never partially loaded. WorldMapState now has a revision, but the map is not integrated, so no cross-system snapshot consistency is claimed beyond facts + inventory. Power-loss durability is unverified (process-kill and fault-injection tests only); the Windows directory flush is a no-op.

entries.title: World map, minimap, compass, waypoint and straight-line navigation (USpnMapSubsystem, map screen, HUD)
entries.gap: Drawing (SSpnMapView) and the screens are verified by the scripted run (Docs/NightBuild01/QA_RESULTS.md), not by an automated pixel test; no hardware gamepad test.

Input routing is covered by automated Slate-injected tests (priority, repeated cycles, input mode after a level travel, console typing with the console put into its typing state); a physical keyboard layout, a real console key press in a focused window and any hardware gamepad are verified only by the scripted OS-input run (Tools/windows/nb01_run_journey.ps1) or not at all. Music/effects volume drive engine sound classes that nothing in the project uses yet.
entries.title: Game flow: main menu, pause, settings, save slots, confirmations, input router (USpnUiSubsystem, USpnSessionSubsystem, USpnSettingsSubsystem)
Doors with states (closed/open/locked/blocked/broken), keys, forcing, light switches and the candidate-based interaction pick (NightBuild04)
entries.gap: The rendered, walked journey through Lvl_SpnBuildingTest is the gameplay validation run documented in Docs/NightBuild04, not an automated pixel test. A pawn standing in the closing door's swing is covered by SpnQA.Doors, not by the headless NightBuild04 tests. No hardware gamepad test (keys are checked by name only).

entries.title: NPC perception (sight with line of sight, wall-attenuated hearing), reactions Idle/Investigate/Alert/Flee/ReturnToRoutine, NPC memory in the save slot (world.npcs), gameplay noises, timed door break-in (NightBuild05)
entries.gap: Patrol (fixed 2026-11-13): a leg is given up after 8 s WITHOUT PROGRESS (before: 8 s leg time, so legs over 12 m never finished); GetPatrolLegsCompleted/GivenUp are checked on the 40 m legs of SpnWorld by SpnWorldQA.Route (npcs_reach_their_routine_points), not on the small NPC test map. Hearing walls (fixed 2026-11-13): an open door leaf no longer counts as a wall (it made the neighbour alarm checks depend on a few cm of the Caretaker's position); the map probe SpnDiag.Npc.AlarmShoutWallProbe (-game on Lvl_SpnNpcTest) lists the obstacles per position. The hearing model still counts straight-line obstacles only (no sound paths around corners). The rendered, walked scenario on Lvl_SpnNpcTest (SpnQA.NpcReaction) is the gameplay validation run documented in Docs/NightBuild05, not a pixel test. The NPC is an engine-shape placeholder without animation; AI Perception is deliberately not used (see Docs/NightBuild05). NPC positions are not saved. Player footsteps (NightBuild06): ASupernaturalProtCharacter sends a Footstep noise every 150 cm on the ground, loudness from the speed (Core FootstepNoiseFor: walk 4 m / 0.15 ... sprint 18 m / 0.6, halved crouched, placeholders), never suspicious on its own: calm NPCs ignore it, wary NPCs do not; an NPC skips its wall traces for noises beyond the range. Surfaces (gravel vs carpet) and shoes do not change it yet. No manual human playtest.

entries.title: Map geometry, road routing, navigation session, NPC memory and the NightBuild03 navigation tech demo (USpnMapSubsystem road mode, ASpnNavDemo)
entries.gap: Road drawing on map/minimap and the 3D demo region are verified by scripted rendered runs (Docs/NightBuild03, demo video), not by automated pixel tests. The demo autopilot is not a vehicle; NpcMemory has no Unreal owner yet.

entries.title: Inventory-backed world pickups and containers
entries.gap: Persistence = the taken flag in world.facts + the inventory section; the actors are recreated from the level / scenario spawner and match their saved state (SpnGame.NightBuild.ObjectsWorld, real level recreation). Core ObjectPersistence (world.objects section, RegionStateCache) is deliberately not integrated: it would duplicate state that world.facts already holds and only pays off with region streaming; see Docs/NightBuild01/COMPLETION_REPORT.md.

entries.title: Exchangeable player character presentation (Docs/Proposals/0013 S1-S3): anim base on the movement state interface, data-driven body/follower presets with mannequin fallback, body height -> mesh scale and camera pivot
entries.gap: 2026-11-24 (NightBuild06) SpnQA.CharacterBody: the automation state was Fail in every run since 2026-11-14 (an engine ensure from GetUsedTextures(EMaterialQualityLevel::Num)) while its QA checks passed - fixed (quality High); -SpnQaBodies=a,b,c now runs every listed body (the parse stopped at the first comma); new rendered check <body>_modular_marker (neutral marker on the shown body visible with the chest exposed, gone under a data-only test vest; screenshots) and gait scenarios walk_to_jog, run_to_sprint, brake_from_run, backward_jog, sideways_jog (measured, not judged). Body collision (NightBuild06): presets may opt in to a capsule that follows the body (Collision=FromHeight / Explicit, Core spn::core::ResolveBodyCollision); the feet, mesh, camera and eye height stay where they are, a larger capsule is refused without room or while crouched / in a ledge move / stepping aside. Default presets keep the capsule (35 / 90): whether the protagonist uses it is the developer's decision (0017). Only the *_fit test presets use it (test_160_fit, test_195_fit, mh_male_193_fit); not replicated (co-op open). 2026-11-15 modular body (Docs/Proposals/0018): USpnWardrobeComponent applies the Core rules spn::core::ResolveCoverage (Tests/Core/BodyCoverageTests.cpp) - separate wearable components, body zone hiding via SpnZone_<zone> material slots (no body mesh is split yet, so nothing is hidden on screen), optional detail geometry only with an enabled category and an exposed zone (only a neutral engine-sphere marker exists, off by default). Not saved, not replicated, no rendered QA yet. 2026-11-15 phase 2 (Docs/Proposals/0017): preset mh_male_193 (local parametric male MetaHuman body, 193 cm, meshes generated by the editor-only USpnMetaHumanPrepLibrary through the public MetaHumanCharacterEditor API; that library is exercised by Tools/character_mh_male_setup.py, not by an automation test). Leg goals blended to the source horizontally (retarget op 'Spn Leg Goals'); sprint row added to BS_Idle_Walk_Run (Tools/locomotion_sprint_samples.py). SpnQA.CharacterBody runs placeholder, mh_template and mh_male_193 (-SpnQaBodies=). 2026-11-14 feasibility phase (Docs/Proposals/0015): the config preset mh_template shows the engine's MetaHuman TEMPLATE body + face, posed by runtime IK retargeting from the hidden mannequin (USpnRetargetFollowAnimInstance); its retargeter is local content from Tools/character_mh_test_setup.py, so on a machine without it the preset falls back to the mannequin and SpnQA.CharacterBody / SpnGame.Character.RetargetedTestBody fail loudly. No facial animation, no grooms, no clothing on the test body. Before that: no final character, no new body asset: the only provider is the template mannequin (ABP_Unarmed reparented to USpnAnimInstance; its graphs still read the template variables, not yet the Spn* variables). Test bodies test_160 / test_195 are a scaled mannequin; the rendered runs use -SpnBody=<preset> with the Doors and World suites (not part of the default suites). Followers are checked headless only (leader pose, attachment, no collision); clipping of real clothing and foot IK are untested because no second skeleton exists. Retarget preparation (0013 section 9, editor scripts, not automation tests): character_skeleton_contract.py (reference contract + candidate checker, verified on the mannequins, a non-human mesh and a missing asset) and character_retarget_prep.py (IK_SpnMannequin, RTG_SpnMannequin_Template in /Game/SpnCharacterPrep, batch dry run Quinn -> Manny: 3 clips with identical frames). NPCs (ASpnNpc) do not use the component yet (0013 S7).

entries.title: Visual build of the placeholder world Lvl_SpnWorld: lighting scenarios, camera runs, landscape import, instanced Megaplants trees
entries.gap: Gameplay route (phase 1, 2026-11-13, Tools/spn_world/gameplay.py): SpnWorldQA.Route plays it with key events (new game through the session, objects exist once, two NPCs on the navigation mesh, encounter and collision, house A key + notebook, house B unlocked with the key, the way to the pine track, save through the session, boundary wall, highway rockfall, play-area guard, main menu -> Load: pose, doors, key, items, NPC memory). Minimap (night build 2026-11-14): SpnWorld installs the generated map data (Tools/spn_world/map_data.py -> Content/SpnWorld/Data/SpnWorldMap.json, USpnMapSubsystem::InstallGeneratedRegion): SpnWorldQA.Route minimap_shows_spnworld checks bounds 1260 m, player inside, no old test POIs visible, a road route to the cabin. Route guide prototype USpnRouteGuideSubsystem (objective line + guide waypoint, derived from saved state): SpnWorldQA.Route guide_step1..4 and guide_completes_at_the_cabin. Texture pop-in warm-up (SpnWorldWarmup, called by the session at New game / loaded pose): exercised by every SpnWorldQA run, its visual effect measured by Tools/spn_visual.ps1 cold still series (Docs/Development/Streaming-PopIn-2026-11-14.md), not asserted. Render resolution (2026-11-13): ASpnWorldLighting sets the PROVISIONAL standard r.ScreenPercentage 90 (TSR) at BeginPlay and restores the previous value at EndPlay, Spn.Quality quality = 100; asserted headless (SpnGame.World...) and in the running world (SpnWorldQA section 'render resolution'); a console r.ScreenPercentage has the higher priority and wins. Graphics settings row 'World render quality' (saved as SpnPlayer/WorldQualityMode, applied live by the world level; Spn.Quality is a session switch that does not change it): headless SpnGame.World.QualityModeFollowsTheGraphicsSetting and the rendered menu check graphics_menu_world_quality in SpnWorldQA. SpnWorldQA.Integration (run_gameplay_qa.ps1 -Suite World) plays the generated world: walking and sprinting on asphalt, forest track and a slope, collisions with a tree, a rock and the cabin wall, the cabin door with E, inside/outside of the room volume, the interior exposure values, the four lighting scenarios switched with Spn.Lighting, camera/feet clipping at the stops. Not covered: the camera runs of USpnCineSubsystem (verified only by the recorded videos of Tools/spn_visual.ps1), USpnWorldBuildLibrary (editor-only, exercised by every world build), the visual result of the exposure (only its configuration is asserted). Earlier note: verified only by real runs: the world generator (Tools/spn_world_build.ps1) and the recorded camera runs, stills and perf reports of Tools/spn_visual.ps1 (videos and PROGRESS.md in Artifacts/VisualProgress). Not part of gameplay: SpnWorldLighting only changes lights/fog/post process of its own level, SpnCineSubsystem only acts with -SpnCine on the command line, SpnWorldBuildLibrary is editor-only, SpnSkinnedGroup is a placement holder for trees. The door opening of the cine walker is logged (SpnCine: walker used door ...) but not asserted.
